title: UST 10-year yield hits 24-year high before strong auctions steady the market
content:
The 10-year UST yield touched about **5.36%** intraday on 7 October, its highest since 2002, as a global bond sell-off accelerated. The 10-year has risen roughly 60bp since the end of July on inflation and energy-price concerns, while the French 10-year yield jumped about 12bp on the day. The Treasury then sold $39bn of 10-year notes at **5.300%**, the highest auction yield since November 2000.

Demand was firm, with above-average non-dealer bidding, and yields retreated from their highs. The 30-year auction on 8 October cleared at about **5.62%**, described as decent but weaker than the 10-year sale. By Friday the 10-year was below 5.25% and US equities posted weekly gains, but elevated term premia remain a risk for global financial conditions.

title: Fed minutes point to another 2026 hike, but October odds fade
content:
Minutes of the Fed's 15–16 September meeting, published on 7 October, showed all participants backed the 25bp hike to a target range of **3.75%–4.00%**, the first increase since 2023. Most officials judged that another rise would likely be appropriate by year-end, with several viewing policy as only mildly restrictive or not restrictive. Some framed the move as insurance against persistent inflation and energy-driven price pressure.

Subsequent data softened the near-term case: futures priced only about a **17–25%** chance of a hike at the 27–28 October meeting, while a December move is seen as more likely. September CPI, due on 14 October, is expected around 3.6–3.7% year on year, and a hot print would keep UST yields under upward pressure.

title: Brent back above $100/bbl as Hormuz tanker attacks and US-Iran tensions flare
content:
Brent crude rose roughly 4–5% on 8 October to around **$105/bbl**, according to Euronews and Oilprice, as Iran stepped up attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz. The Pentagon reportedly told US Central Command to finish preparations for a possible resumption of major combat operations, although no date has been set and President Trump said talks with Iran were productive. Earlier in the week prices had fallen after G7 members agreed to tap emergency stockpiles.

Brent eased to about **$103–104/bbl** on 9 October as hopes of progress in the talks returned. Sustained high energy prices feed inflation expectations and have been cited as a driver of the global bond sell-off, so headlines on Hormuz remain a key swing factor for rates and central banks.
